questions.q: What is the capstone project's OLTP source database?
options: AdventureWorks2012
AdventureWorksDW2014
Northwind
tempdb
questions.explain: The capstone extracts from AdventureWorks2012's transactional tables — Sales.SalesOrderHeader, Sales.SalesOrderDetail, and Production.Product.

questions.q: Why does the capstone create new Capstone*-prefixed tables in AdventureWorksDW2014 instead of writing into the existing FactInternetSales/DimProduct tables?
options: So the capstone's own load can't collide with or corrupt the real tables this catalog's other courses already query
Because AdventureWorksDW2014 doesn't actually contain a FactInternetSales table
Because SSIS is physically incapable of writing to a table that already has data in it
Because surrogate keys only work in tables with 'Capstone' in the name
questions.explain: Writing into a clearly-labeled, dedicated set of tables keeps the capstone's own data safe from — and safely separate from — the real DimProduct/FactInternetSales tables other lessons in this catalog rely on.

options: AdventureWorksDW2014's existing dbo.DimDate table
A brand-new DimDate table you create yourself
AdventureWorks2012's Sales.SalesOrderHeader.OrderDate column directly
It doesn't join to anything — dates are stored as plain text
questions.explain: AdventureWorksDW2014 already ships a correct DimDate table with an integer, yyyymmdd-format DateKey — there's no reason to build a new one for this capstone.

questions.q: Why does CapstoneFactOrderSales store ProductKey instead of the source system's ProductID?
options: ProductKey is a warehouse-generated surrogate key, decoupling the fact table from the source system's own business key
ProductID doesn't exist in AdventureWorks2012
SSIS destinations reject any column named ProductID
ProductKey and ProductID are simply two names for the exact same value
questions.explain: Storing a surrogate key instead of the raw business key is standard dimensional modeling practice, and it's what CapstoneDimProduct's lookup exists to resolve.

questions.q: Which chapter's concepts does this four-lesson capstone pull together?
options: All of Chapters 1 through 8 — control flow, data flow, variables, error handling, incremental loads, and deployment
Only Chapter 1's introductory material
Only the data flow transformations from Chapter 4
None of the previous chapters — the capstone introduces entirely new concepts
questions.explain: The whole point of a capstone is synthesis — this project is deliberately built to use control flow, data flow, variables/parameters, error handling, and the incremental-load pattern all in one package.
